ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part II.1; Business Corporations Act (Alberta), R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, ss. 21.1-21.3 (Register of Individuals with Significant Control); Business Corporations Act (Canada), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 21.1, as amended by the Budget Implementation Act, 2023, S.C. 2023, c. 26; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 24; FINTRAC Interpretive Guidance on Politically Exposed Persons (2024)
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — Alberta ISC register and federal CBCA beneficial ownership register are not publicly searchable; access is granted to law enforcement, CRA, FINTRAC, and provincial securities regulators; the corporation must maintain and produce its own register to directors, shareholders, and prescribed authorities upon request

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled passport or certified government-issued ID copies of every incorporator, director, officer, and 25%+ significant-control individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or Commissioner for Oaths in the individual's country of origin; apostille by the designated competent authority of the relevant Hague Convention state (Global Affairs Canada for Canadian-origin documents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (entered into force for Canada on January 11, 2024); consular legalization required for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Certificate of Incumbency, Certificate of Good Standing, and constitutional documents of the ultimate parent chain (ByteDance Ltd. / TikTok entities) evidencing the 25%+ UBO chain of ownership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating registry (e.g., Cayman Islands General Registry, HKSAR Companies Registry) and licensed corporate service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus certified English translation where the source record is not in English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and sworn source-of-funds declaration supporting the initial capitalization of the Alberta corporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution of the subscriber or contributing shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and apostille, or verified direct banker's confirmation routed to Alberta counsel; subject to FINTRAC record-keeping and retention rules

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of each director, officer, shareholder, and UBO against (i) OFAC SDN List inclusive of the 50% Rule aggregation, (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) Canada's Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, (iv) Canadian criminal-record and adverse-media indicators, and (v) enhanced PEP checks recorded as a flag in the ISC register pursuant to FINTRAC Guidance. Negative-match screening evidence must be archived for at least five years and made available to the Registrar or FINTRAC upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) — NUANS name search and online filing administered through the registrar's authorized service-provider network; for federal CBCA entities deploying a registered office in Alberta, name clearance is obtained through Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (www.ic.gc.ca/corporations)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate name must comprise a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', or 'Incorporée'. English and French are equally permissible; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. A purely provincial Alberta name has no bilingual requirement, but a federal CBCA name may trigger bilingual obligations where the name is subject to geographic or public-policy restrictions. The name must not be confusingly similar to any active or pending NUANS record.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Foreign Bank, Trust, Loan, Insurance, Assurance, Broker — prior regulatory authorization required under the Bank Act (Canada) and Alberta financial institutions legislation
University, College, Institute (tertiary education) — prior consent of the Minister of Advanced Education (Alberta) required
Engineering, Engineer, Professional Engineer — consent of APEGA (Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta) required
Cooperative, Co-op, Credit Union — approval required under the Cooperatives Act (Alberta) or provincial financial-institutions legislation
Royal, Crown, Government, Canada, Canadian, RCMP — Crown or ministerial consent required; any name implying Crown connection or official government status is prohibited

Obscene, scandalous, or otherwise objectionable terms, and any name that appears to condone an act punishable by law — mandatory statutory prohibition under s. 12 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
Identical or confusingly similar names to existing trademarks or NUANS records — refusal or post-registration opposition by the intellectual-property rights holder is possible
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS name search report is valid for 90 days from issuance. Upon rejection, the applicant must obtain a fresh NUANS report and resubmit the articles online through the Alberta Corporate Registry or its authorized service provider; a written reconsideration request may be lodged with the Registrar of Companies attaching the fresh report and arguments of distinctiveness. If the Registrar still refuses, the aggrieved person may apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for a name-change order under s. 12(3) of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). For federal CBCA names, reconsideration may be requested from the Director General of Corporations Canada, followed by judicial review in the Federal Court of Canada filed within 30 days of the final decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only where a licensed registered-agent service maintains a physical street address in Alberta accessible for service of process during normal business hours; a mail-forwarding-only PO Box address is non-compliant. For a TikTok Shop e-commerce seller without Canadian personnel, a virtual office can satisfy the legal registered-office test but materially weakens the commercial-substance position for Canadian corporate residence; CRA may reassess the corporation as resident in Canada and taxable on worldwide income. A service provider offering meeting-room access and physical custody of corporate records is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-Risk standard: approximately 5% annual probability of a CRA desk or field audit leading to an unannounced physical premises verification. The probability escalates to approximately 15-20% if transfer-pricing, non-resident UBO concentration, related-party TikTok commission payments, or thin-capitalization markers appear in the first two GST/HST and T2 corporate filings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended — incorporation and articles (ss. 11–12); registered office (s. 101); corporate records (s. 102); by-laws (s. 128).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (online portal: www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed; the Corporation may incorporate with CAD 1 of nominal capital. No escrow or blocked-deposit account is required for a general e-commerce retail corporation; share subscription proceeds are credited to the securities register upon issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Corporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) is accepted; THAT, the subscription agreement for the initial allotment of shares is ratified, and share certificates be issued to the founding shareholder; THAT the registered office of the Corporation be established at [registered office address in Alberta] and the records office be maintained thereat; THAT the proposed by-laws be adopted as the by-laws of the Corporation; THAT [Name] be and is hereby appointed President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer until successors are elected; AND THAT the directors are authorized to execute all documents and open bank accounts, including TikTok Shop payout and Wise B2B settlement accounts, as necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via authorized NUANS search agents; online at www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS search for up to three proposed corporate names in the prescribed format, including a phonetically identical check. If a distinctive word name is desired, file the Name Reservation Request and pay the reservation fee; alternatively incorporate as a numbered company (e.g., '12345678 Alberta Ltd.').
required_dossiers: List of up to three proposed corporate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name is refused due to conflict with an existing corporation or trademark, select the next available name from the same NUANS report and re-file; an applicant may appeal a refusal to the Registrar of Companies within 30 days if the refusal is considered erroneous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (online portal or in-person service counter), or an authorized corporate services provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute Form 1 Articles of Incorporation specifying the corporate name, registered office address within Alberta, authorized share capital (classes and rights), restrictions on share transfers (if any), and number of first directors. Deliver the executed form, director consents, and the prescribed fee to the Registry; retain the filing acknowledgement and work order number.
required_dossiers: Form 2 — Consent to Act as Director for each initial director
Proof of payment of the incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a compliance query, correct the identified deficiency in the Form and resubmit promptly; an administrative refiling resets the review timeline and does not forfeit priority where the name reservation remains valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the Form 1, the Registrar endorses the Articles and issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which marks the creation of the corporation. Record the Corporate Access Number, acquire a corporate minute book, and confirm the registered office and records office address in the corporate register.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued by the Registrar)
Endorsed copy of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a clerical error is detected in the certificate or articles, submit an application for Correction of Articles to the Registry under the ABCA; a corrected certificate is issued without affecting the incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Governance — First Board Resolution and By-laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (written consent resolution permissible under the ABCA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first directors' meeting or execute a written consent: adopt By-law No. 1, confirm the registered office, ratify the share allotment and subscription, appoint officers (President, Secretary, Chief Financial Officer), and approve the opening of the TikTok Shop payout and Wise B2B settlement bank accounts.
required_dossiers: First Board resolution signed by all directors
By-law No. 1 and supporting governance policies
Share subscription agreement and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any invalidity in a director resolution caused by quorum or notice defects may be cured by a subsequent unanimous written consent of all directors; the Secretary records the cure in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Alberta Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency — Business Registration Online portal; Alberta Minister of Finance (integrated corporate-tax administration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register the Corporation with the CRA through the Business Registry (or myBA) to obtain the 9-digit Business Number, corporate income tax account (RC0001), GST/HST account (RT0001), and payroll account if applicable. Confirm the Alberta address for tax notices and register any provincial levy accounts administered by the Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and director particulars
Banking rail confirmation (TikTok Shop seller account and Wise B2B details)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the registration due to a replication error in the registry feed, re-submit the application through CRA's Business Registration Online telephone service with the work order number; corrections to entity type or address are processed using the CRA RCAC form.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not statutorily applicable for pure online social-commerce retail (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110). Conditionally applicable: municipal business licensing (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Business License Unit) and Alberta Municipal Affairs / Safety Codes Authority for any leased office or warehouse.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license is required for the virtual TikTok Shop retail activity; conditional municipal Business License, Development Permit, or Home Occupation Permit may apply if the operator uses a physical office or residential address for storage or pickup. The TikTok Shop Platform Seller Agreement supplies contractual seller verification, not a government license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) — Environmental Assessment and Regulatory Assurance Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full EIA or registration certificate is required for e-commerce retail absent industrial operations; registration under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (RSA 2000, c E-3) is triggered only if a fulfillment or warehouse operation crosses Schedule 1 thresholds (e.g., refrigerated storage ≥ 1,500 m³ or qualifying waste-management activities).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source air or wastewater discharge is authorized from a pure office or retail operation; any future warehouse must comply with municipal sewer-use by-laws, the Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives for VOCs and particulate matter, and the Recycling Regulation (AR 190/1997) requiring diversion of cardboard, pallets, and single-use packaging once weekly waste volumes exceed prescribed limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for pure virtual operations. Conditional clearance for physical premises: (i) fire-safety inspection and a Certificate of Occupancy from the local Safety Codes Authority under the Alberta Building Code; (ii) structural inspection for mezzanine or racking loads; and (iii) workplace-safety clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code (AR 87/2009), including first-aid provision, hazard communication, and incident-reporting obligations once employees or contractors are present on site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and My Business Account; Alberta corporate services: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) via Service Alberta; provincial corporate income tax administered by CRA under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act collection agreement
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Canadian-incorporated social-commerce company: (1) incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Alberta Business Corporations Act via the Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES); (2) in the same CRA Business Registration Online session, obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) with a federal GST/HST program account for the Alberta permanent establishment — instant digital issuance, no capital required; (3) open the provincial corporate tax account (Alberta) and payroll (RP) account if hiring; (4) for a non-resident foreign seller with no Canadian presence: submit Form RC1 together with foreign incorporation charter, foreign tax ID and Certificate of Residency (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for US entities), along with a designated Canadian representative address; CRA mails the BN/GST-HST account number within 1–2 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime; Canada uses statutory elections under the Income Tax Act and Excise Tax Act, including: s. 85 rollover election on asset transfers, s. 249.1 non-calendar fiscal-period election, s. 45(2) principal-residence/capital-gains election, s. 18.2 net-revenue election and s. 18.5/18.6 hybrid-mismatch elections under the EIFEL rules; GST/HST Quick Method election (Form GST74) and GST/HST annual-filing election (Form GST22A) are available for qualifying e-commerce retailers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal GST (Goods and Services Tax) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; no HST/PST in Alberta
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 for resident small suppliers over four consecutive calendar quarters (ETA s. 240); zero threshold for non-resident suppliers and marketplace/distribution-platform operators (2021 simplified digital-services framework)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate, no digital stamping, and no compulsory e-invoicing API; CRA accepts electronic records and voluntary PEPPOL-style e-invoices; the seller must maintain machine-readable sales/export data and file GST/HST via CRA My Business Account (NETFILE/GST/HST) with export documentation retained for CRA audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods is zero-rated under s. 5, Part V, Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act when goods leave Canada within 60 days (up to one year where justified) and the seller retains proof of export; offshore services to non-registered non-residents are zero-rated under ss. 7 and 8, Part V; TikTok Shop cross-border sales to foreign end-consumers are zero-rated, while domestic Canadian sales attract 5% GST (no Alberta provincial component).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA CAED/G7 or Canadian Export Declaration)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no standalone statutory FX-repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark reflects prudent documentation practice, otherwise CRA reassessment window is four years (unlimited in cases of misrepresentation or fraud); incomplete export files cause retroactive loss of zero-rating and reassessment at 5% GST, plus compounding daily interest; gross negligence or false-statement penalty is 25% of the net tax deficiency (ETA s. 285); fraudulent evasion carries fines up to CAD 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to five years (ETA s. 327).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the monetary authority and issuer of legal tender; it does not administer exchange controls. Prudential regulation of banks is vested in the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Bank Act (Canada) S.C. 1991, c. 46; AML/ATF surveillance and reporting-entity supervision are administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) S.C. 2000, c. 17; payments infrastructure is operated by Payments Canada (Lynx RTGS, ACSS, Real-Time Rail). The Minister of Finance retains policy authority over the Investment Canada Act and the Special Economic Measures Act for sanctions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full and unrestricted convertibility on both current and capital accounts. The Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951; as an IMF Article VIII member since 1951, Canada imposes no exchange controls and no central-bank authorization requirement for inward or outward transfers, trade settlements, repatriation, or dividend remittance. The Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) and Bank of Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. B-2) preserve legal-tender status only; the CAD/USD rate is market-determined and floating. Capital-account profit remittance by a TikTok Shop retail entity is legally unrestricted; practical hurdles are tax-borne only: Part XIII withholding tax on dividends to the non-resident parent is 25% statutory, reduced to 10% under the Canada-China Income Tax Agreement (1986) where the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 10% of voting shares; interest remittance is 10% and royalties 10% under the same treaty. NR4 information returns and T106 non-arm's-length reporting apply. Inbound acquisitions by a WTO investor require Investment Canada Act net-benefit review only where the enterprise value threshold is met (approximately CAD 1.32-1.33 billion for 2024-2025), which a retail social-commerce entity will not approach; no review is required for a de novo Canadian corporation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender requirement for export or platform-settlement proceeds. A Canadian resident may hold, repatriate, and convert 100% of export receivables and TikTok Shop settlement proceeds without Bank of Canada or FINTRAC approval. The only binding reporting obligations are (i) FINTRAC large virtual-currency/EFT transaction reporting and cross-border currency reporting thresholds (CAD 10,000) administered operationally by banks and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), and (ii) Statistics Canada's Canadian Direct Investment surveys for in/outward foreign direct investment positions; neither imposes limits on timing or conversion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High as a supplementary settlement rail, Low as primary treasury custody. Wise B2B (Wise Payments Canada Inc.) and Payoneer are FINTRAC-registered Money Service Businesses permissible for receiving TikTok Shop settlement payouts and making low-to-mid value cross-border disbursements; they are not authorized under the Bank Act to take demand deposits from the public, do not provide CDIC coverage (CDIC insurance covers only chartered bank member deposits up to CAD 100,000 per depositor per institution), and their fund-holding models require segregation without re-lending. Legal constraint: an operational balance held at an MSB exposes the entity to custodial risk beyond OSFI-regulated prudential supervision; the treasury blueprint must therefore route TikTok Shop payouts into a Wise/Payoneer collection wallet and sweep balances daily via SWIFT/ACH into the Schedule I concentration account. The entity itself does not require MSB registration under the PCMLTFA because it uses payment processors for its own trade flows, not for third-party money services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not a statutory requirement in the FINTRAC regime; remote video-KYC verification is legally permitted for an Alberta corporation and is accepted by most Schedule I banks for Canadian-resident signatories. However, in practice, cross-border treasury onboarding with non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (Chinese parent) will trigger enhanced due diligence, and banks will normally condition the Capital Escrow Account opening on at least one in-person signing session at the Calgary or Edmonton commercial banking centre for the designated signing officer, ideally the Canadian-resident director/CFO. Non-resident directors cannot be assumed to be acceptable as sole signatories. The Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA) board-residency quota (at least 25% resident Canadian directors for boards of four or more; at least one for boards below four) should be satisfied by appointing a Canadian-resident director/manager empowered to attend interviews and manage banking conduct. Pure remote opening is feasible where the bank accepts a 'banker's confirmation' from the parent's home institution plus a notarized, apostilled corporate record package (Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Status from the Alberta Corporate Registry, articles, by-laws, directors' resolution, and the derivative register), but this route typically adds 10-15 business days and a higher compliance-review tier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party settlement (TPS) opacity: TikTok Shop payouts arrive from an offshore platform entity (e.g., TikTok Pte. Ltd., Singapore, or TikTok LLC, US) rather than directly from end-consumers, creating an unclear payer-counterparty chain for the bank's transaction-monitoring engines.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) 12 months of TikTok Seller Center payout statements; (ii) the executed TikTok Seller Remittance and Settlement Terms; (iii) a reconciliation file matching platform settlement batches to the account-entry ledger; (iv) a flow-chart memorandum from Canadian counsel mapping the platform remitter to the Alberta entity; (v) a completed merchant-beneficiary confirmation from the TikTok payout processor (Payoneer/Wise); and (vi) a statutory declaration of merchant-account ownership signed under the Alberta Evidence Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO and source-of-funds opacity for the inbound equity injection from mainland China: the bank will classify the parent as high-risk absent SAFE/ODI evidence and will require full source-of-funds verification before releasing escrow balances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble (i) notarized share register and UBO schema for every natural person holding >10% of shares; (ii) Alberta Corporate Registry Certificate of Status and current Annual Return printout; (iii) share subscription agreement approved by directors' resolution; (iv) Chinese outbound-investment clearance evidence (MOFCOM certificate and SAFE FX registration where applicable) with the remitting bank's transfer voucher; (v) 12 months of audited bank statements of the parent; (vi) source-of-funds statutory declaration compliant with FINTRAC expectations; and (vii) a confirmation that no person is listed under the Canadian Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) consolidated autonomous sanctions list, OFAC SDN, or the Canadian Criminal Code money-laundering watch database.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party trade supply chain to Chinese goods suppliers: high volume of payables to offshore related suppliers can trigger trade-based money-laundering red flags (over/under-invoicing, split payments, non-arm's-length pricing).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (i) supplier master list with Chinese unified social credit codes; (ii) six months of purchase orders, commercial invoices, bills of lading, and CBSA customs entries demonstrating physical goods flow; (iii) intercompany transfer-pricing documentation and a CRA-compliant arm's-length study; (iv) automated sanctions/PEP screening results for all suppliers; (v) the bank's trade-services questionnaire with confirmatory warehouse/logistics contracts; and (vi) an internal AML compliance program document satisfying the PCMLTFA compliance-program obligation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Chargeback and refund volatility in live-commerce operations: elevated dispute/refund ratios can breach account covenants and expose the bank to merchant-acquirer regulatory reporting under the retail payment chargeback framework.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) TikTok Shop dispute-resolution SLA and refund-window policy; (ii) a 12-month gross chargeback ratio report targeted below 1.0%; (iii) a refund-timing waterfall forecast; (iv) processor holdback statements (Payoneer/Wise reserve balances); (v) pro-forma monthly cash-flow modeling with stress scenarios; and (vi) a board-approved refund reserve policy maintaining a liquidity buffer of no less than 30 days of expected refund liabilities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name-matching and sanctions residue across the payout and disbursement chain: ordinary Chinese supplier names, shared surnames, or transliteration matches to listed entities will generate false positives requiring manual clearing before wires are released.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare (i) an automated name-screening report comparing all known counterparties against the SEMA consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, and Canada's Criminal Code offender database; (ii) a documented remedial name-match analysis with resolution of each positive hit; (iii) beneficial-owner declarations from each high-volume supplier; (iv) confirmation of legal-entity identifiers (LEI where available); and (v) a standing instruction authorizing the bank's compliance team to share screening results directly with counsel to compress clearing cycles.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Canada does not operate a transaction-level FX purpose-code registry (unlike PRC SAFE or certain Asian jurisdictions). The operative discipline is: (i) execute a SWIFT MT103 from the parent/remitting bank to the Capital Escrow Account at the chosen Schedule I bank, using field 72 remittance narrative 'SHARE SUBSCRIPTION - [Alberta Entity Name]' or 'INTERCOMPANY LOAN - [Loan Agreement Date]' as the substitute purpose code; (ii) support the wire with a board-resolutions package evidencing share issuance or loan authorization; (iii) where funding is equity, update the Alberta share register and file the Articles of Amendment if any share-class changes are made; (iv) where funding is a shareholder loan, execute a written intercompany loan agreement at an arm's-length rate consistent with the CRA prescribed quarterly rates, and observe thin-capitalization limits (ITA s. 18(4) debt:equity of 1.5:1 for specified non-resident shareholders; the EIFEL limitation applies only to groups with substantial net book equity, which this entity will not reach); (v) convert CAD/USD freely at the bank's spot desk, with no OSFI/FINTRAC approval barrier; and (vi) for amounts arriving as settlement rather than capital, route through the TikTok Payout Collection Sub-Account and sweep daily to the operating account. For cash physically crossing the border in excess of CAD 10,000, CBSA Form E677 reporting applies; interbank EFT/MT103 wires do not require CBSA declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (i) cross-border supplier payments in USD/CNY via SWIFT MT103 to the beneficiary's bank, with remittance narrative matching the commercial invoice number; (ii) documentary credit financing via Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) governed by UCP 600 and ISP98 where applicable, particularly for first-time Chinese supplier relationships, with an advising/confirming bank in China and Incoterms 2020 (FOB/CIF) terms; (iii) domestic Canadian disbursements through Lynx for same-day high-value CAD transfers and through ACSS/EFT for threshold-batch payments, including CRA remittances (GST/HST - 5% federal, with no Alberta provincial sales tax, and payroll source deductions) via the CRA's electronic payment rails; (iv) US-dollar disbursements through the bank's US correspondent network (Fedwire for same-day USD, standard ACH for low-value); and (v) regular sweeps from the Wise/Payoneer collection wallet to the Schedule I concentration account via MT103 executed at least daily. The treasury control design should maintain a target concentration balance equal to 45 days of operating expenditure in CAD and 30 days of supplier payables in USD, with all excess swept into an interest-bearing treasury deposit subject to CDIC coverage planning across institutions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla USD/CAD FX forwards (OTC, ISDA 2002 Master Agreement plus Credit Support Annex, tenors 1M-24M) - the standard hedge for committed US-dollar trade payables and TikTok settlement surpluses
FX swaps (USD/CAD rollover structures) - used for cash-flow timing mismatches between inbound settlement and outbound supplier payment dates

Vanilla FX options, including zero-cost collars and participating forwards (3M-12M tenors) - permissible and preferable when the entity wants rate-certainty elimination with upside preservation, subject to IFRS 9 hedge designation
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CAD, long-dated 1-5 years) - permissible for matched asset-liability hedging where the entity enters into committed multi-year purchase agreements

CAD/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs referencing the CNH fixing) - permissible for hedging Chinese supplier CNY payables where onshore deliverable CNY market access is not established; deliverable CAD/CNY forwards may also be transacted through the offshore CNH market at the bank's discretion. CAD/USD NDFs are technically available but functionally redundant given full convertibility and the liquid deliverable market, and will not typically be offered as a cost-effective instrument

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each incorporation anniversary date, not the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive anniversaries allows the Registrar to dissolve the corporation administratively; the corporation is placed in arrears after the anniversary date and may be struck off without further notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal and Alberta Corporate Income Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporate taxation year-end; for a December 31 year-end, due by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equals 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of default up to 12 months; repeat failure may double the penalty; prescribed interest is compounded daily; directors may be assessed personally for unremitted source deductions and related taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly and quarterly filers must file within one month after each reporting period; annual filers with gross revenue under C$400,000 must file within 3 months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is 5% of the unpaid net tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeat late-filing within a 3-year period increases the penalty to 10% plus 2% per month; daily prescribed interest continues to accrue.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold applies under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. A mandatory independent audit is required for distributing corporations and for any corporation whose shareholders, meeting the statutory minority threshold, demand an auditor appointment. Otherwise, shareholders of a private corporation may waive the audit by unanimous resolution or unanimous consent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS applies to publicly accountable enterprises; private retail corporations may apply Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) in the CPA Canada Handbook, with the option to elect IFRS. Tax returns require Canadian GAAP information adjusted to taxable income on the T2.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not require a separate annual UBO registry filing; the annual return confirms only active status, registered office, and current directors. Share transfers must be approved and recorded in the corporate records, and directors must update the register upon any change. If the entity is incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act, a register of individuals with significant control must be maintained at the registered office and updated within 15 days of a change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 100 - 250 per year for a registered office and registered agent in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - 10,000 for a full audit of a small private retail corporation, depending on transaction volume and corporate complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general corporate tax rate (15% federal Part I + 8% Alberta provincial; Alberta no general tax holiday)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-Controlled Private Corporation (CCPC) Small Business Deduction reducing combined rate to 11% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income (9% federal + 2% Alberta); SR&ED investment tax credits (15%-35%); accelerated capital cost allowance for digital/e-commerce assets. Non-resident-owned corporations are ineligible for SBD.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T2 (Corporation Income Tax Return), filed electronically via CRA-approved EFILE/Netfile software or CRA My Business Account; Alberta corporate tax is collected through the T2 under the CRA-Alberta tax collection agreement; mandatory electronic filing where gross revenue exceeds CAD 1 million.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal period may not exceed 53 weeks)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be filed within 6 months after fiscal year-end. Final tax balance due within 2 months after year-end; 3 months for CCPCs claiming the SBD. Quarterly tax installments required if prior-year federal+provincial tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) for income tax purposes after adding/deducting GIFI adjustments from financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Canadian-source business income attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment (PE) plus any worldwide income; where a treaty PE threshold is not met, file a T2 only if Canadian-source income is subject to Part I tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: Line 100 less non-capital loss carryforwards (20-year forward, 3-year back), capital loss deductions, and treaty-protected amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only Canadian deductions reasonably allocable to the Canadian PE; attach Schedule 102 for cross-border related-party transactions and Schedule 91 if treaty benefits are claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal basic tax on taxable income, computed as federal rate (38%) less provincial abatement (10%) less general rate reduction (13%), yielding the 15% net federal headline rate on general corporate income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Federal abatement is limited to income earned in a province; non-residents without a Canadian PE do not receive the abatement and therefore report federal tax at 38% minus applicable general rate reduction, subject to treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance due or refund: total federal and Alberta provincial tax payable less installment payments, credits and withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File this line to compute the final Part I liability; any excess Part XIII withholding on dividends, royalties or interest is claimed through Form NR7-R (reduction of tax withheld) rather than Line 800 unless a full T2 is filed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% for each full month of delay, up to 12 months (max 17%); gross negligence penalty: 50% of understated tax; daily compound interest on all unpaid amounts at CRA prescribed rate; late installment penalties apply under s. 161. Directors may be liable for unpaid corporation tax where the return fails to report source deductions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% federal Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder; Alberta imposes no separate provincial dividend withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty-reduced dividend rates (e.g., 5% under Canada-US treaty on shareholders owning at least 10% of voting shares; 15% otherwise), the non-resident recipient must provide the Canadian payer with a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC), completed Form NR301 (or NR302/NR303 for full/partial exemption), and a beneficial-ownership certification before each payment. The payer retains these documents to justify the reduced rate; where the full 25% was withheld, the non-resident must claim a refund via Form NR7-R or by filing a T2 return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate: 25% on interest and royalty payments to non-residents. Treaty relief (e.g., Canada-US Convention): interest typically 10% (0% for arm's-length related-party interest qualifying under paragraph 212(1)(b)(vii); some treaties provide 0-15%); royalties 10% for patent/copyright; advertising and know-how fees are generally treated as business profits and may be tax-exempt if no Canadian PE. A recipient must show economic entitlement and beneficial ownership; back-to-back or conduit royalty structures are attacked.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Schedule 102 (International Transactions) must be filed with the T2 when the aggregate fair market value of cross-border non-arm's-length transactions (of the taxpayer) exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in the fiscal year; full contemporaneous Local File documentation is mandatory at the same threshold. Master File is required where the MNE group has consolidated revenue of at least CAD 1 billion and the Canadian entity's reportable transactions exceed CAD 5 million for intercompany financial transactions or intangibles, or CAD 20 million for other tracked transactions (Income Tax Act s. 233.7).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone CARICOM/UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the income tax system enforces substance requirements through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR, s. 245), transfer-pricing allocation of profits based on functions/assets/risks (s. 247), and treaty beneficial-ownership doctrines. A 'letterbox' TikTok Shop entity in Alberta—without employees, physical operations, real management authority, or business decision-making substance—risks re-characterization, reallocation of profit to the foreign parent, denial of treaty benefits, and a 25% GAAR penalty on any resulting tax benefit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully failing to report TikTok Shop sales revenue; fabricating invoices; using undisclosed offshore shell accounts for settlement payouts; knowingly making false statements or omissions in the T2 return or GST/HST filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of not less than 50% and not more than 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, plus up to 5 years imprisonment on indictment (2 years less a day on summary conviction); civil gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the understated Part I tax and 50% of unremitted GST/HST; daily compound arrears interest; CRA may seize bank accounts and accounts receivable under the Income Tax Act and Excise Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable under s. 227.1 of the Income Tax Act for the corporation's unremitted source deductions (employee withholdings) and GST/HST (s. 323 ETA); a director who authorizes or participates in evasive filings faces criminal prosecution, imprisonment, confiscation orders, and travel restrictions imposed by the court as bail or probation conditions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Conduit Arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting TikTok Shop platform fees, management charges, royalty or commission rates outside the arm's-length range; failing to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation or file Schedule 102; operating through paper 'conduit' entities in zero/low-tax jurisdictions to strip Canadian profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reprice the transaction and assess the full arm's-length adjustment; a 10% penalty under s. 247(3) applies to the net transfer-pricing adjustment where the taxpayer failed to make reasonable efforts; interest runs on the reassessed amount; GAAR penalty of 25% of the tax benefit will be imposed if the avoidance transaction is found to be abusive. Master File non-compliance attracts CAD 1,000 daily penalty for each full day of failure, minimum CAD 1,000 up to CAD 24,000 (per subsection 233.7(8)).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: For deliberately incomplete or misleading TP dislosures, directors who directed, authorized, or acquiesced in the mispricing are exposed to criminal prosecution for tax evasion and to civil liability for the 10% TP penalty and the GAAR penalty to the extent they personally participated; CRA can pursue director assessments where the corporation fails to remit the assessed amounts for unremitted withholdings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using TikTok Shop payouts and Wise B2B payment rails for settlement, while failing to register as a Money Services Business (MSB) if the corporation is in the business of retaining or transferring funds; failing to maintain AML compliance policies; failing to report Suspicious Transactions or large virtual-currency/cash transactions to FINTRAC; laundering proceeds of fraudulent or unreported online retail sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalty up to CAD 2,000,000 per violation for a financial entity/jurisdictional deposit taker under the PCMLTFA; criminal conviction for deliberate non-registration or non-reporting can result in fines up to CAD 500,000 plus imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment; FINTRAC can also publicly name non-compliant entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for FINTRAC penalties, but a director who knowingly directs deception or money laundering schemes under the Criminal Code or PCMLTFA faces personal prosecution, seizure of proceeds, imprisonment up to 10 years for money laundering, and restrictions under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act affecting cross-border travel.
